newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 30.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Industrial sales in June had a real increase of 11.2 percent. The largest increase was in manufacturing of means of transportation, year-on-year by more than 60 percent. The largest decrease was in the tanning industry, where companies had a decline in sales of about one fourth. Direct flood damages in industry are estimated at 9.66 billion crowns.
- Vaclav Havel visited Usteckoorlicka, one of the areas affected by the floods, yesterday and tried to awaken interest of residents in working on repairing damages.
- Parliament Vice-chairman Karel Ledvinka said the surplus in next year's government budget should be around 40 billion crowns.
- The Industry and Trade Ministry estimates direct damages to electricity, heating, gas and coal companies at 1.49 billion crowns.
- Ceskomoravsky Penzijni Fond had half-year profits of more than 50 million crowns.
- The crown continued to drop yesterday to as far as 18.830 against the mark.
- The Regional Development Ministry will propose the cabinet support housing in areas affected by the floods by providing 750 million crowns to build 1,500 flats.
- Pension funds Allianz-Hypo and Zivnobanka PF will merge by the end of August.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Letov, which should supply wings and rear hulls to Aero Vodochody for L-159 turbo-jets, will be liquidated due to billions of crowns in debts and blocked accounts, the company said.
- Domestic insurance companies should pay more than 10 billion crowns to their clients for flood damages. Ceska Pojistovna alone expects to pay five billion.
- India's automobile maker Eicher backed down from its plan to manufacture Felicia automobiles with Skoda Volkswagen in India.
- The engineering giant Skoda Plzen had audited losses last year of more than 190 million crowns. For the second time, shareholders will not receive dividends.

- ZVU Hradec Kralove, which met with large debts in the last few months, offered to pay creditors 35 percent of the amounts owed in order to avoid bankruptcy. The court has already approved the plan, and now only shareholders have to agree.

PRAVO - The third degree flood watch in Breclav was cancelled yesterday when the level of the Kyjovec river decreased by 30 centimetres in 24 hours. That was the last district with a third degree watch.

- The Supreme Investigation Office found out after its latest inspection of income-tax bases for companies that 40 subjects decreased their tax base without authorisation by a total of more than 200 million crowns.
- Liechtenstein's Blax Corporation, the majority owner of Poldi Steel, approves of the entry of Mossei International Holding into Poldi with an equal amount of voting authority.
- Due to floods, Trinecke Zelezarny had losses of 200 million crowns, primarily due to stopped production and problems in railway transport.
- Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl is currently preparing material for the cabinet to reevaluate the significance of the import deposit system for the trade balance.

- Despite a slight decline from 28.7 percent to 26.1 percent in July, the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) are still nearly five points ahead of the Civic Democratic Party, which has 20.4 percent, according to Factum.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Yesterday, Czech-Austrian Ronja opened the largest duty free shop in Europe at the border crossing Hate u Znojma. The space of 300,000 square metres includes not only two duty free shops, but also a shopping centre, several restaurants, a petrol station and a race track.
- Chemopetrol Litvinov signed a contract with American Farrel worth more than three million pounds to supply new granulation lines for manufacturing polypropylene.
- The Senate economic committee yesterday recommended to return the law for value added tax to parliament and approved a number of proposals for changes to the law.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
